meta.title: Frely CLI — Give Claude Code, Codex and pi the Frely Skill
meta.description: Frely CLI installs the frely Skill in agents with a shell, such as Claude Code, Codex and pi. Your agent uses your Frely account, installs Skills and Agents, and adds FrelyMCP when a task needs it. Web ChatGPT connects through FrelyMCP.
meta.socialDescription: Give your agent the Frely Skill. One prompt installs Frely CLI, signs you in and installs the Skill.
hero.release: frely Skill · for agents with a shell
hero.description: Paste one prompt into Claude Code, Codex or pi. The agent installs Frely CLI, signs you in with an email code and installs the frely Skill. With the Skill, your agent uses your Frely account, installs Skills and Agents from the Store, and sets up FrelyMCP when a task needs another computer.
principles.label: Project highlights
principles.mcp: Remote MCP + OAuth for web clients
workflows.description: Add the device MCP in your client and complete OAuth authorization. Pick a common client below, or follow one of the two universal methods.
workflows.label: Agent client list
tools.note: Clients of one device share its workspace and managed processes. File tools respect the workspace; shell commands run with the device OS account’s permissions, without a workspace sandbox.
agents.label: INVOKE FRELY-HOSTED AGENTS
agents.description: Install a published Frely Agent as a trigger Skill in your client and invoke it through Frely CLI.
agents.note: Authorize calls with your account or a restricted API key. Your client's model provider configuration stays in place; hosted Agent calls require no device execution permission.
models.label: LOCAL MODELS / PROVIDERS
models.description: Connect a running Ollama or another loopback OpenAI-compatible runtime as a personal Frely Provider. Use it through your existing Frely Access Points and API keys.
models.note: Requires a running local model and an empty, active personal Provider slot. Local MCP execution requires separate authorization.
install.runtime: Standalone installers include their runtime and do not need Node.js.
install.node: Requires Node.js 22+. Then run frely login and frely skill install.
source.description: Frely CLI and this page are open source. Explore the code, report an issue, or contribute a change.
source.note: The CLI connects to Frely’s hosted Relay service. The open-source client and local MCP runtime are licensed under Apache-2.0; use of Frely trademarks is subject to the trademark policy.
footer.note: Give your agent the Frely Skill
copy.failure: Copy unavailable. The command is selected; use your device’s copy action.
tools.connect: Add the fixed address https://mcp.frely.cloud/mcp. It is the same for every device on your account and contains no access token. Each calling client signs in with your Frely account through OAuth.
tools.verify: Ask the agent to use the Frely workspace_info and list_directory tools. Check that the returned folder and names match the target computer. The command-line agent's built-in shell runs on the calling computer.
tools.diagnostics: Use frely doctor for configuration and connection status, or frely doctor -v for diagnostic details. A real tool result from the target computer verifies the client-to-device connection.
install.diagnostics: Need to check the connection? Run frely doctor on the controlled computer. Add -v for detailed diagnostics.
nav.productsCliNote: Connect a computer to Frely from the terminal
clients.trademark: Client names and logos belong to their respective owners and appear here only to indicate compatibility.
clients.urlAudience: For clients such as ChatGPT that accept a pasted URL.
clients.urlStep1: Open your client's “Add MCP server / apps & connectors” settings.
clients.urlStep2: Paste the URL below and choose OAuth as the authentication method.
clients.urlStep3: Sign in with your Frely account in the browser to authorize.
clients.jsonTitle: Option 2 · Paste a JSON config with a token
clients.jsonAudience: For clients such as WorkBuddy and Doubao Work that cannot run the OAuth sign-in and only accept a pasted MCP JSON config that carries a Bearer token.
clients.jsonStep1: Open your Frely devices page. Under Controllers, choose Add device, then the “Copy JSON config (Bearer token)” tab.
clients.jsonStep2: Generate the token, confirm with your passkey or authenticator code, and copy the config. The token is shown only once.
clients.jsonStep3: Paste the copied config into the client's MCP settings (WorkBuddy: ~/.workbuddy/mcp.json) and save. No browser sign-in is needed.
clients.jsonShape: The sample shows the shape only. Use the config copied from the devices page, which contains your real token.
clients.animLabel: Animated walkthrough: create a token config on the devices page and paste it into WorkBuddy
device.description: Agents use MCP to access the computer you authorize. Frely forwards tool calls and returns execution results.
device.browserTitle: Give browser agents access to your device.
device.browserDescription: Add your device MCP URL in ChatGPT Web or another compatible client. Authorize access and ask the agent to inspect projects, edit files or run commands.
device.browserExample: “Read this project’s README and summarize how to run it.”
device.computerTitle: Give command-line agents access to your device.
device.computerDescription: Use Codex, Claude Code or another command-line agent on a different computer to access the target computer's files, command-line tools and processes through MCP.
device.computerExample: “Use the Frely tools to check the build on my workstation.”
device.targetTitle: Your agent sends the task. Your device runs it.
device.targetDescription: Files · Shell commands · Managed processes. Your device makes an outbound connection to Frely; no public listening port or router configuration is needed.
device.compatibility: Requires a remote HTTP MCP client with OAuth support. Device permission and client authorization are separate. Keep the controlled computer running and online.
more.description: Use local model sharing or invoke Frely-hosted Agents when you need them. Device access requires neither setup.
more.title: More uses for Frely CLI
install.agentPrompt: Install Frely CLI and the frely Skill on this computer. On macOS or Linux run curl -fsSL https://frely.cloud/install.sh | sh; on Windows PowerShell run curl.exe -fsSLo "$env:TEMP\frely-install.ps1" https://frely.cloud/install.ps1; powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\frely-install.ps1". Ask me for my email, run frely login --email <my email>, ask me for the 6-digit code from the email, then run frely login --code <code>. Then run frely skill install --host <your host: claude-code, codex, pi or generic> and read the Skill it installs. Do not run frely mcp start until I ask for it.
relation.eyebrow: FRELYMCP · FOR CLIENTS WITHOUT A SHELL
relation.description: Web ChatGPT and Claude cannot run a shell, so they cannot use the Skill. Add FrelyMCP as a connector. FrelyMCP is the path for working on another computer, driving a connected browser and using Cloud MCPs you bought.
relation.cliDescription: Runs on this computer, receives tool calls and returns results.
relation.relay: MCP + OAuth · relayed by Frely · outbound connection only, no public port on the device
relation.chatApps: ChatGPT · Claude on the web, and other clients with remote MCP support
relation.chatExample: “List the files changed recently in my workspace.”
relation.step1: You send a message in the chat app.
relation.step2: The agent calls Frely tools through MCP; Frely forwards the call to your device.
relation.step3: Frely CLI runs it on this computer, and the result returns to the conversation.
